title: Australian Hearing Health Population Simulator — Communication Vocabulary
purpose: A controlled, extensible vocabulary for representing communication modalities, preferences, signed languages, visual and written supports, environmental preferences, assistive technology, interaction strategies, accessibility accommodations, contexts, barriers and profile metadata in a synthetic population simulator.
scope_note: This is a project vocabulary for research modelling. It is not a clinical coding system, diagnostic taxonomy, validated psychometric instrument, prevalence dataset or substitute for consultation with Deaf, Deafblind and hard-of-hearing communities.
design_principles: Keep preferences, capabilities, requirements, identity, environmental conditions, strategies, barriers and outcomes as distinct concepts.
Do not infer communication preference, language proficiency, identity or comprehension from audiometric hearing category, age or device use.
Treat an unrecorded preference as unknown or not assessed, not as absence of need.
Allow multiple and context-dependent communication methods.
Record the person's own stated preference wherever possible.
Distinguish a technology being owned, available, used, preferred, requested and beneficial.
Do not treat sign languages as interchangeable or assume written English substitutes for a signed language.
Record environmental conditions separately from an individual's profile.
Record communication outcomes separately from environmental opportunity and preference alignment.
Support changes over time and preserve the provenance of each observation.

status_values.not_assessed: The attribute has not been assessed or asked.
status_values.not_applicable: The attribute does not apply in this context.
status_values.declined: The person chose not to provide the information.

source_values.observed: Observed in a defined interaction; not necessarily a stable preference.
source_values.assessed: Recorded through a specified assessment; name the assessment and date.
source_values.proxy_reported: Reported by an authorised or agreed proxy; identify the relationship and basis.
source_values.scenario_assigned: Assigned by an experimental scenario; not a claim about a real person.

term_record_schema.label: Human-readable term
term_record_schema.attribute_type: Preference, capability, requirement, modality, environmental support, context, barrier, strategy or metadata
term_record_schema.value: Recorded value, separate from the term definition
term_record_schema.valid_from: Optional date/time from which the record applies
term_record_schema.valid_to: Optional date/time until which the record applies

domains.label: Communication modalities
domains.description: Methods through which a person sends, receives or exchanges information.
terms: Using visible speech movements and facial cues to support understanding.
Receiving information primarily through auditory input.
Exchanging short written messages through SMS or messaging applications.
Using visual information to communicate or understand messages.
Using facial expressions as part of communication.
Communicating through a natural or established signed language.
Representing words or names using manual alphabet forms.
Receiving or exchanging information through touch.
Combining two or more communication modalities.

domains.label: Spoken and auditory communication preferences
domains.description: Preferences about how spoken communication is delivered. These are preferences, not evidence of ability.
terms: Prefers spoken interaction in the relevant context.
Prefers individual conversation rather than group interaction.
Prefers communication in a small group.
Prefers a natural speaking volume rather than shouting.
Prefers alternative wording when information is unclear.
Prefers missed information to be repeated.
Prefers speakers to signal topic changes.
Prefers one person to speak at a time.
Prefers to know the subject or agenda in advance.

domains.label: Signed languages and signed communication
domains.description: Specific signed languages and tactile/visual forms. Record the actual language and proficiency separately.
terms: An English-based signed communication system; not interchangeable with Auslan.
An international contact signing system used in some cross-language settings.
A named sign language other than Auslan; record its name separately.
Individually or family-developed signs used in a particular setting.
Adapting signing position and visual field to the recipient.
Tactile interaction involving guided or shared hand contact; specify the person's preferred approach.
A Deaf interpreter who may work alongside a hearing sign-language interpreter.
A qualified interpreter between a signed language and another language.

domains.label: Visual communication supports
domains.description: Visual conditions and resources that may support communication. Availability does not establish comprehension.
terms: The communication partner's face is visible.
Lighting permits the face and relevant visual cues to be seen.
The person can see the communication partner or relevant visual information.
Relevant people, objects, locations or demonstrations are visible.
Important details are also supplied in writing.
Diagrams or illustrations support the explanation.
Pictures, symbols or visual sequences support information.
Speech is captioned in real time.
Important events or notifications are signalled visually.
Appointment details are displayed or supplied in an accessible written/visual format.

domains.label: Written communication and language preferences
domains.description: Written-language preferences and formats. Language proficiency must be represented separately.
terms: Prefers straightforward language and limited unnecessary jargon.
Uses or prefers English for written communication; does not itself indicate proficiency.
The person's preferred language for written information; store the language value separately.
Prefers information using simplified text and supportive images or layout.
Prefers headings, lists and clearly organised written content.
Prefers sequential instructions supported by images or diagrams.
Prefers or requires information translated into a specified language.
Uses more than one language; record each language and proficiency separately.
Requires or prefers interpreting between spoken languages in a specified context.

domains.label: Environmental communication preferences
domains.description: Preferences about the physical and social environment. Actual environmental measurements belong to interaction records.
terms: Prefers competing noise to be reduced.
Prefers a comfortable, relatively close speaking distance.
Prefers spaces with suitable acoustic characteristics.
Prefers adequate lighting for visual access.
Prefers seating that supports visual access to communication partners.
Prefers fewer participants in group communication.
Prefers a familiar or predictable communication setting.

domains.label: Assistive listening and communication technology
domains.description: Technologies used, available, requested or preferred. Distinguish ownership, access, use, benefit and preference.
terms: Uses, has access to, or prefers hearing-aid technology; specify which status applies.
Uses or has access to cochlear implant technology; do not infer performance.
Uses or prefers a bone-conduction hearing device.
Uses or prefers a remote microphone system.
Uses or prefers an induction loop system.
Uses or prefers an FM assistive listening system.
Uses or prefers an infrared listening system.
Uses real-time conversion of speech to text.
Uses an application to convert speech into text.
Uses Australia's National Relay Service; record the relevant service mode separately.
Uses visual, vibrating or other alerting technology.
Uses a board or display containing words, symbols or pictures.
Uses AAC methods or devices to supplement or replace speech.

domains.label: Communication interaction strategies
domains.description: Actions that a person, communication partner or service provider may use. Record who initiated the strategy.
terms: Establish the person's attention before beginning.
Face the person while speaking where appropriate.
Avoid covering the mouth where visual speech cues are relevant.
Use different wording to clarify a message.
Repeat information that was not received.
Check whether the intended information was understood.
Invite the person to explain key information in their own words.
Provide important information in writing after the interaction.
Use a strategy to resolve a communication breakdown.
The listener asks for additional or clearer information.
Allow breaks during demanding or lengthy communication.
Involve a support person when requested or agreed.

domains.label: Accessibility and individual support requirements
domains.description: Supports requested, required or agreed for a particular person and context. Do not infer them from age or hearing category.
terms: Professional interpreting support is requested or required.
A Deaf interpreter is requested or required.
A nominated support person assists communication, with the person's agreement.
Allow additional time to receive, process or respond to information.
Provide strategies or adjustments to manage communication-related fatigue.
Adapt communication for identified cognitive accessibility needs.
Adapt communication to address visual access needs.
Provide an agreed Deafblind-specific communication method or support.
Provide digital information in an accessible format.

domains.label: Communication contexts
domains.description: Contexts in which preferences, capabilities, supports and barriers may differ.
terms: Communication with friends and social networks.
Communication at work or in employment-related settings.
Communication in school, training or tertiary education.
Communication through video calls or meetings.
Communication with government or public services.
Communication in urgent or emergency situations.
Communication in community settings and activities.

domains.label: Communication barriers and difficulties
domains.description: Barriers observed, reported or experienced in an interaction. A barrier is not a personal deficit.
terms: Competing environmental noise interferes with communication.
Overlapping speech makes communication more difficult.
The speaker's face or mouth cannot be seen.
The communication partner is too far away for the chosen method.
The listener reports difficulty understanding an accent.
The speaking rate is difficult to follow.
Jargon or complex language impedes understanding.
A requested or required interpreter is unavailable.
Device, connectivity, platform or digital-literacy issues impede access.
The languages used do not adequately match the person's language needs.
A partner is unaware of or does not respond to stated communication needs.
The person reports fatigue associated with communication effort.
Insufficient time is available for accessible communication.
The setting does not permit the person's preferred communication method or disclosure.

domains.label: Preference and profile metadata
domains.description: Metadata used to record the source, certainty, context and temporal validity of profile information. These are schema fields rather than personal preference terms.
terms: The person's stated preferred method for a defined context.
Another method the person is willing or able to use.
A preference that applies only in a defined context.
Preferred number or size of communication participants.
Language preferred for a specified communication task.
A person the individual prefers to communicate with or have present.
Confidence or certainty associated with the recorded preference; define scale separately.
Whether the information was self-reported, observed, assessed or supplied by an authorised proxy.
Date the preference was last reviewed.
A recorded change in preference over time.

implementation_notes: The current AgentProfile.communication_preferences list should not be expanded to hold all vocabulary domains. It should eventually be replaced or supplemented by structured profile records.
A separate language profile should record language name, modality, proficiency, literacy where relevant, and evidence/source. Do not infer proficiency from preference.
A separate technology record should distinguish ownership, access, use frequency, preference, requested use and reported benefit.
Interaction-level environment fields such as noise, distance, face visibility and written information availability belong to CommunicationEvent or its environment object.
Communication barriers should be recorded as event observations or person-reported experiences, not permanent attributes by default.
The current acoustic indicator is illustrative and must not be interpreted as speech intelligibility or comprehension.
Preference compatibility should return supported, not_supported or unknown, and should not determine comprehension.
For real-world research, review the vocabulary with Deaf, Deafblind, Auslan-using, hard-of-hearing and other relevant community representatives before use.

evidence_and_governance.evidence_status: Initial taxonomy informed by general communication-access guidance and hearing-health literature; individual terms require source mapping and community review before being described as evidence-validated.
recommended_reference_families: World Health Organization guidance on communication with people who are deaf or hard of hearing.
NSW Health guidance on engaging Deaf consumers, Auslan and Deafblind communication access.
American Speech-Language-Hearing Association guidance on aural rehabilitation and communication access.
Australian Government guidance for accessible primary care and interpreter use.
Peer-reviewed research on communication barriers, listening effort, healthcare access and Deaf community experiences.
evidence_and_governance.citation_policy: For publication, attach an exact source citation to each term or group of terms. Do not claim that the whole vocabulary is validated merely because its domains are informed by published guidance.
